data.title: Fanatics names Afterpay as preferred BNPL partner
data.description:
Sports apparel and merchandise retailer Fanatics has named Afterpay as its preferred partner for buy now, pay later (BNPL) payments processing.

The move means that shoppers across Fanatics’ ecommerce sites can now use Afterpay’s “Pay in 4” and “Pay Monthly” offerings. Pay in 4 allows consumers to make their purchases and then complete their payments in four installments over six weeks, without interest. Meanwhile, Pay Monthly allows consumers to complete payments over 24 months for purchases from $100 to $20,000.

Fanatics websites include:

  • Fanatics.com
  • Lids.com
  • NBAStore.com
  • NHLShop.com
  • Other associated partner sites

Fanatics is No. 13 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Fanatics is also No. 132 in Digital Commerce 360’s new AI Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Why Fanatics is working with Afterpay on BNPL

“Afterpay gives our customers the flexibility today’s shoppers expect, so fans can support their teams and celebrate the biggest moments in sports,” said Tucker Kain, chief strategy and growth officer at Fanatics, in a statement. “This feature allows us to further our mission to relentlessly enhance the fan experience, whether that’s through the personalized discovery Fanatics Ads brings to shopping, the live energy of Fanatics Fest, or the flexibility Afterpay offers at checkout, and make our world-class assortment of products available and accessible in more ways than ever before.”

The retailer and Afterpay had already established a relationship that included partnering for Fanatics Fest in summer 2026. Fanatics Fest is a multi-day sports, collecting and cultural festival. In 2026, Fanatics held it at the Javits Center in New York City.

“Being selected as Fanatics’ preferred BNPL partner is a meaningful milestone for Afterpay as we continue expanding into high-intent shopping categories where flexibility matters,” said Tanuj Parikh, head of revenue for Cash App and Afterpay. “Fanatics sits at the center of sports culture, bringing fans closer to the teams and athletes they love. Together, we’re offering fans more flexible options at checkout while supporting one of the most dynamic commerce ecosystems in sports.”

Block, Inc. (formerly Square, Inc.) fully owns Afterpay. It also owns:

  • Bitkey
  • Buzz
  • Cash App
  • Proto
  • Square
  • Tidal
  • Weebly

Afterpay framed the partnership as underscoring its “continued momentum with leading retail, fashion, lifestyle, and commerce brands as more merchants look to meet customer demand for flexible payment options.”

It added that fans can expect to see Afterpay and Fanatics partner in more ways going forward.

data.title: Hills Distribution adds PexUniverse for HVAC ecommerce expansion
data.description:
Hills Distribution and PexUniverse have announced a partnership, expanding each company’s role in distributing parts in the heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) space.

Hills Distribution describes itself as a platform of independent plumbing, HVAC and hydronic distributors. PexUniverse describes itself as an ecommerce distributor for plumbing, heating and HVAC parts and supplies.

Hills Distribution also referred to the partnership as a “transaction” in its announcement. The companies did not disclose financial terms in their announcement.

Additionally, Hill Distribution said two existing team members, Vitaly Kharitonov and Mariya Pylypyuk, would remain with PexUniverse, with Kharitonov in an unspecified role and Pylypyuk serving as PexUniverse’s general manager after the transaction.

Hills Distribution noted that Pylypyuk would continue “to lead the business alongside the existing management team.”

Why Hills Distribution tapped PexUniverse for an HVAC ecommerce expansion

“Hills Distribution is excited to welcome PexUniverse to the platform and deepen our presence in the ecommerce channel, which continues to gain momentum across our industry,” said Ron LaBusch, CEO of Hills Distribution, in a statement. “PexUniverse has built an impressive business with a differentiated value proposition and moat, and we see meaningful opportunities to accelerate its growth while strengthening the broader Hills platform.”

PexUniverse said it has a catalog of about 8,000 SKUs that it offers from its distribution facility.

The partnership adds PexUniverse to a list of Hills Distribution brands that also includes:

  • Plimpton & Hills
  • Coastal Supply Group
  • RJ Murray
  • Bender Plumbing Supply

Hills Distribution framed the partnership as expanding its “presence in a digital channel that continues to gain share within the plumbing and HVAC distribution industry.” It also complements Hills Distribution’s branch network while “creating meaningful opportunities,” according to the company.

“PexUniverse brings a differentiated capability to Hills and expands our participation in one of the fastest-growing channels within plumbing and HVAC distribution,” said Jon Perry, chairman of Hills Distribution. “The business has developed a broad product offering and an efficient digital model that complements our existing companies.”

Gennady Sharovetky, former owner of PexUniverse, said it was important to find a partner that understood what made his business successful. He said Hills Distribution and Grove Mountain Partners share PexUniverse’s focus on scaling its business and long-term growth.

Grover Mountain Partners is a private investment firm involved in the transaction. It said it invests in wholesale distribution and blue-collar services companies with annual revenues between $25 million and $300 million.

data.title: Trane Technologies adds AI tools for repairs and part replacements
data.description:
Trane Technologies is expanding its artificial intelligence (AI) offerings for building owners and facilities teams, including a new maintenance platform designed to centralize equipment records and maintenance workflows and help inform repair and replacement decisions.

The heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) and climate control equipment manufacturer announced that the offerings will span building analytics, maintenance management, connected controls and thermal management.

“As building operations become more connected and more complex, we’re evolving our AI and digital portfolio to help customers operate with greater clarity and control,” said Chris Tanaka, vice president of product management at Trane Technologies.

Trane Technologies’ Maintenance Manager

Maintenance Manager centralizes all the pieces that go into facility management. The company said it connects work orders, asset records, repair history and supporting documentation in one system.

Trane Technologies said it enables better coordination between service teams and more informed decisions about whether to repair aging equipment or begin planning for replacements.

“With Trane Cloud Analytics and Maintenance Manager, customers can connect building data, service workflows and asset history to support earlier action, better coordination and more informed planning,” Tanaka said. “Across the broader portfolio, these new solutions extend that same approach into controls and system management to help customers improve performance and reduce waste over time.”

The rest of Trane’s new product suite

And beyond Maintenance Manager, the Sept. 17 announcement covers several other tools.

Trane Cloud Analytics gives teams access to performance trends and efficiency gaps from connected building equipment. The company also designed a new Cloud Connected BACnet Thermostat to bring cloud-based building management to light commercial buildings that don’t have a full-building management system in place.

Tracer Zone Sensors are designed to simplify installation and setup for new construction and retrofit projects, and AI Control for Water Systems adjusts chiller plants to improve efficiency across existing infrastructure.

For data centers specifically, the announcement includes Chiller Plant Management and Data Hall Team Control. Both are designed to coordinate climate control over complex environments.

“As data center growth drives higher cooling loads, tighter performance requirements and faster response expectations, thermal management is becoming increasingly integral to uptime, efficiency and long-term infrastructure strategy,” said Oakley Roberts, president of data centers at Trane Technologies. “Intelligent, coordinated cooling systems are becoming essential to operating modern AI and mission-critical infrastructure at scale. These innovations help customers improve available capacity, strengthen resilience and maintain consistent thermal performance as computing demands continue to accelerate.”

How Trane got here

Trane has invested in AI technology for years. In 2024, Trane Technologies acquired BrainBox AI.

BrainBox AI is a Montreal-based company that had developed an AI platform to predict energy needs and automate HVAC operations. That acquisition built on a two-year collaboration between the companies. It also brought BrainBox’s predictive control capabilities directly into Trane’s product development pipeline.

In 2025, Trane opened a dedicated BrainBox AI lab and showroom focused on AI and energy management in buildings.

The investment in AI has occurred alongside growth for Trane. In its most recent fiscal quarter ended June 30, bookings were up 39% year over year. Meanwhile, net revenue grew 11% over the same period, to $6.35 billion.

data.title: Ecommerce Trends: How Best Buy is using AI
data.description:
Best Buy is pushing artificial intelligence (AI) into areas of its operations in 2026, and its leadership team has described wider ambitions for how Best Buy will use AI to achieve near-term objectives.

In March, while speaking at the UBS Global Consumer and Retail Conference, Best Buy CEO Corie Barry called AI “a huge enabler of growth,” as well as for “good employee experiences.” At the time, she was addressing AI tools as internal resources for solving team members’ own problems. However, she also outlined how certain use cases will extend to customers as well.

Shoppers-facing AI deployments have since followed, notably with Best Buy opting to leverage OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

Best Buy ranks No. 8 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

Best Buy is also No. 200 in Digital Commerce 360’s AI Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

How Best Buy is using AI internally

What is Best Buy’s Ask Blue shopping assistant?

In August, Best Buy detailed how it was rolling out its new customer-facing shopping assistant, Ask Blue. Jason Bonfig, senior executive vice president, chief customer and product and fulfillment officer at Best Buy, told analysts on the retailer’s Q2 earnings call that Ask Blue brought together multiple areas of expertise to enable outcomes for shoppers.

“Speaking of online experiences, I’m excited to announce the launch of Ask Blue, our new conversational AI shopping and support assistant,” he said during the call. “It brings together expertise from across Best Buy’s website in one easy-to-use experience.”

Altogether, Bonfig characterized Ask Blue as added value for online shoppers.

“It combines product knowledge, support, resources, customer reviews, availability and pricing to help customers make informed decisions,” he assessed. “Ask Blue will help customers figure out what tech is right for them.”

He cited examples such as comparing products, identifying important differences, checking compatibility and getting additional support. That may include connecting the shopper with a human support specialist.

Best Buy web sales by year

How Best Buy is working with OpenAI on agentic commerce

In addition, Best Buy has eyed new ways for online shoppers to discover its product listings through AI channels.

“We’re also continuing to partner with AI companies like OpenAI to make sure we are showing up in the places where our customers look for technology and advice,” Bonfig noted on the August earnings call. He is scheduled to replace Barry as Best Buy’s CEO on Nov. 1.

Bonfig described Best Buy’s recent “commerce integration with OpenAI,” which the company is promoting among its holiday plans for discovery and gift-buying.

“Customers can now discover products, receive recommendations and complete purchases for Best Buy directly within ChatGPT,” Bonfig told analysts. “We view this as an important step in expanding our digital ecosystem and positioning Best Buy at the forefront of emerging AI-enabled commerce experiences.”

data.title: La Joya Jewelry navigates channels, rising costs in its fulfillment
data.description:
As a retailer with high-value products, La Joya Jewelry is in a fortunate situation to be able to weather changes in fulfillment costs, according to founder Nishit Mehta.

La Joya sells exclusively online, through a mix of its direct-to-consumer (DTC) website and through Amazon and Walmart’s marketplaces. Founded in 2020, the retailer sells lab-grown diamonds with its products.

By channel, La Joya’s average order value (AOV) varies significantly. When selling on Walmart, for instance, the jeweler’s AOV is about $150 to $160, Mehta shared. However, on Amazon, La Joya’s AOV is about $375. Both fall short of La Joya’s AOV on its DTC website, which is about $1,500.

He guessed that the difference could stem from consumers on Walmart and Amazon looking for bargains or cheaper gifts. On the retailer’s DTC site, he said, consumers treat their purchases more seriously. They’re often searching for an expensive piece in general or an engagement ring specifically.

How La Joya Jewelry handles multi-channel order fulfillment

For orders through its DTC website, La Joya ships from its own office as well as using Amazon’s fulfillment. Its sales through Amazon and Walmart use those marketplaces’ fulfillment services.

“Amazon’s backend allows you to do multi-channel fulfillment,” Mehta told Digital Commerce 360. “So we just go ahead and tell them that this product needs to be shipped to XYZ. They make sure it goes in a non-Amazon package so the customer doesn’t know. Our packaging is consistent throughout whether you buy from Amazon or from the website. So as far as the customer is concerned, it could be shipped from our own offices.”

He added that La Joya stocks “a lot of goods” with Walmart, which also offers multi-channel fulfillment.

“Walmart — I don’t know whether it’s customer-centric or the jewelry business is not yet matured,” he said, referring to the lower AOV through that channel. “So while we do stock a lot of goods there, we don’t find in the holiday season people wanting that kind of jewelry. So we tend to use that a little less.”

When the marketplaces aren’t fulfilling on the retailer’s behalf, it mainly uses FedEx and the U.S. Postal Service (USPS), with occasional DHL deliveries, Mehta explained.

USPS filed at the end of August to increase delivery prices throughout the 2026 holiday shopping season. The carrier anticipates the rates taking effect at midnight on Oct. 4, remaining in place until midnight on Jan. 17, 2027.

Mehta noted that La Joya communicates its cutoff shipping dates “boldly” on its website. It also uses its email marketing and social media presence to spread that message.

Impact of rising fuel costs on jewelry delivery

He noted that La Joya has absorbed the impact of rising fuel costs so far this year.

The price of a barrel of crude oil has risen to about $102, as of Sept. 10. For comparison, it was about $66 when the United States and Israel began their war with Iran at the end of February, according to historical data from Trading Economics. It had also reached a high this year of about $112 per barrel in April. That increase in oil costs has led delivery carriers to raise costs, adding surcharges to cover their expenses.

In April, Amazon added fuel and logistics surcharges. That followed USPS’ shipping surcharge, which it announced in March. Also in March, FedEx chief customer officer Brie Carere said the carrier adjusts its fuel surcharge index weekly and that it’s “doing its job.” That is, it has helped FedEx to avoid “material impact” from the war, according to Carere.

Meanwhile, at La Joya, “frankly, we’ve taken the hit because it was kind of priced in anyway,” Mehta explained. “We are selling $1,200, $1,500 products. $30 going to $35 or $38 doesn’t really break anything. So we just take the hit and go ahead. As far as the marketplaces are concerned, they have very good rates in terms of shipping.”

Additionally, La Joya insures all its products and requires an adult’s signature upon delivery to avoid losing deliveries.

“Having said that, it does get lost very often, but at least it’s insured, so there’s no loss on either side,” he said.
